context: Use the bundled `edge-cases` corpus, whose entire contents are as follows. Its keyword list, in order, is: alpha, beta, gamma, delta, epsilon, zeta, eta, theta, iota, kappa, lambda, mu, translation, machine translation. The 17 papers, each with the zero-based indices of the concepts it mentions, are: edge.1 [0,1]; edge.2 [0,1]; edge.3 [0,1]; edge.4 [0,2]; edge.5 [0,2]; edge.6 [1,2]; edge.7 [1,2]; edge.8 [1,2]; edge.9 [2,1,2]; edge.10 [12,13]; edge.11 [12,13]; edge.12 [12,13]; edge.13 [12,13]; edge.14 [12,13]; edge.15 [3,8]; edge.16 [5,6]; edge.17 [4,7,9]. A paper contributes every pair of its distinct concepts, with a repeated concept counted once (so edge.9 contributes only the beta-gamma pair), except the nested pair (12,13), translation with machine translation, which is excluded from the pair stream. A pair's count is the number of papers holding both concepts. The corpus is deliberately small: it contains pairs at exactly min_count, min_count minus 1 and min_count plus 1, and two once-seen pairs that collide with a frequent pair under the bundled hash rows, so sketch estimates can exceed true counts. The sketch may use at most 16 hash rows; candidates are ranked by estimate, highest first, ties by concept-name order. Submit each qualifying pair once with its two concept names in lexicographic order.
